memory_candidates.content: First-order k-types over a finite monadic signature (KType sig k = NormalForm sig k 0 -> Bool) do NOT compose under Kleene star: 'has a factorization into pieces of type sigma' is not a depth-k' property for any fixed k', and cut-type pairs are a depth-(k+1) datum, so a periodic repetition of one literal segment can realize family triples the source colouring lacks (the cut-pair obstruction). The substitute that works for ultimately-periodic-witness arguments in this tree: a finite 'sigma-star profile' of a finite word -- its k-type plus, for every sigma, the relation {(type p, type q) : w = p ++ m ++ q, m in L_sigma^*} -- which composes under concatenation by an explicit four-case law (middle inside left, inside right, straddling at a piece boundary, straddling inside one piece), paired with a 'cut profile' (set of (profile prefix, profile suffix) pairs). Infinite Ramsey for pairs (Nat.exists_strictMono_const_pair_colour) on the colouring (profile, cutProfile) of stretches gives consecutive blocks whose periodic repetition has tail-type set contained in the original's; pigeonhole on cut pairs bounds piece lengths by Nat.card(Profile)^2. No automata, no idempotent, no order-reversal lemma (mirror once per orientation, as exists_zFactorization does).
